To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
HSV-1 infection of human fiboblasts activates the expression of a number of interferon-responsive cellular genes.
infection of human cells by HSV-1 induces expression of a number of cellular genes whose expression can be induced by interferon.
HSV-1, like HCMV, induces the expression of cellular genes that are normally induced by interferon.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular basis of the induction of interferon-responsive gene transcription in human fibroblastic cells infected with HCMV and HSV-1.
the induction of cellular gene expression by viruses.
the induction of interferon-responsive gene transcription by infection with HCMV or HSV-1 and the mechanism through which the induction is brought about.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
HSV-1, but not HCMV, activates interferon-responsive genes through a mechanism that is not interferon-dependent.
infection of human cells by HSV-1 results in activation of a subset of cellular interferon-inducible genes, and that this is mediated by a mechanism other than the classical interferon pathway.
infection with HSV- 1 activates cellular interferon-responsive pathways in human fibroblastic cells.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
HSV-1, as well as HCMV, activates the expression of cellular interferon-inducible genes.
HSV-1 induces the expression of a number of cellular interferon-inducible genes.
infection of human cells by HSV-1 results in activation of the cellular interferon-responsive pathway, although the degree and the extent of this activation are less than that seen with HCMV.
The main takeaway from our work is that
HSV-1, a DNA virus, can induce the expression of cellular interferon responsive genes, although the degree to which it does so is less than that of a DNA virus such as HCMV.
HSV-1 induces interferon-responsive genes in the absence of interferon.
infection with HSV- 1 induces the expression of cellular genes in the absence of interferon.
